question.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ for $t>0.$

current_example.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $\mathbf r(t) = \left\langle 2\sin t, \:2\cos t \right\rangle.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $\mathbf T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $\mathbf{r}(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
\mathbf \kappa(t) = \dfrac{\left\| \mathbf T'(t) \right\|}{\| \mathbf r'(t) \|}
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate $\mathbf T'(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
